gaps.sentence: All ___ must wear identity badges at all times on site.
gaps.explanation: 'Personnel' = the employees of an organisation; 'personal' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: Could I ___ your pen for a moment?
gaps.hint: meaning: take and return later (from someone's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Borrow' means to take something temporarily; 'lend' means to give something temporarily to someone else.
'Complement' means to combine well with or complete something; 'compliment' means to praise.

gaps.sentence: She is ___ of hearing after years beside the speakers.
gaps.explanation: 'Hard of hearing' is the fixed phrase; 'hardly' is an adverb.

gaps.sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
gaps.hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
gaps.explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.

gaps.sentence: There is little ___ that the plan will be approved.
gaps.hint: pattern: little ___ that something will happen
gaps.explanation: 'Possibility that ...' is the standard pattern; 'opportunity' means a situation that lets you do something.

gaps.sentence: We sat ___ to the sound of the waves.
gaps.explanation: 'Listen to' means to pay attention to sound deliberately; after 'sat' the -ing form is needed.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
